title: Prelude: The Board Before the Game, 1694–1896

sections.brief: Open the volume in the City of London: what the Corporation is (Lord Mayor, Court of Common Council, its own police, privileges preserved by exception in Acts of Parliament), then its three documented oddities in order: the business vote (about 32,000 business votes against about 9,000 residents in April 2013, per the Green Party, with the Bloomberg survey), the Remembrancer seated in the Commons (budget reported at about £6 million; Shaxson's 'oldest institutional lobbyist'; Caroline Lucas's 2013 request), and the Temple Bar ceremony (the 1869 'requiring' account against the carriage passing without stopping). Present the 'sovereign city-state' claim and the record side by side: less autonomy than Jersey, Guernsey or the Isle of Man, Parliament legislates for it, and the Corporation's own 'rather like a trade body' is the finding. End on why the chapter starts here: a legislature with a seat for finance, inside the state that would later issue the Balfour Declaration (one line, link forward). Figure: comparison of the claim and the record.

The three enclaves laid side by side as legal facts: the City (privilege without sovereignty), Vatican City (sovereign only from the Lateran Treaty of 11 February 1929, 44 hectares, compensation for the Papal States lost in 1870), and the District of Columbia (Article I, Section 8; Home Rule Act of 1973; about 700,000 residents with no voting member of Congress). Then the 'empire of three cities' claim, stated in its own words, and why no treaty, charter or shared body supports it; name plainly how the claim slides into older tropes about hidden rulers. Keep the 1929 and 1973 facts brief and say they belong to later volumes. Figure: comparison table, four columns at most (enclave, legal basis, what is documented, what is not).

Why the chapter's clock starts in 1694. Tell in order: the Stop of the Exchequer (2 January 1672; about £1.2–1.3 million in obligations; the goldsmith-bankers ruined), William III's war with France, and the Bank of England chartered on 27 July 1694 (£1.2 million lent at 8% by 1,268 subscribers in 11 days; Paterson's proposal and Montagu's role, both given); then what the Bank became: 'banker to the Government' and manager of the National Debt, the 1844 note-issue law, and the debt of about £1 billion (more than 200% of GDP) at the end of the Napoleonic Wars. The mechanism is the point: state borrowing from private subscribers through a chartered company in the City, the structure the banking houses of the next sections lent into. Figures: a money chain (subscribers, the Bank, the 8% loan, the Crown's war, taxpayers servicing the debt) and key figures.

The board between 1789 and 1815: the Napoleonic wars, the crowns, the Church and the dynasty. Tell Mayer Amschel Rothschild's rise from the Frankfurt Judengasse (court factor to Hesse-Kassel, 1769; the 1806 custody of the Landgrave's fortune; the 1812 will) and the five-sons dispersion, then the peak and the decline after 1901, using every deep-dive section on rothF; give the comparison with the Barings, Warburgs and Bleichröders and the capital estimate of £8–10 million around 1875 as the deep dive gives it. Introduce each state piece (Britain, France with emancipation in 1791, Russia with the Pale of 1791 and about two million emigrants 1881–1914, the Ottoman Empire 1516–1917, the Papal States) briefly, linking forward: the Ottoman story to rd0_ottoman, the Edmond material in rothP to bc_s04, and Walter Rothschild and the Balfour letter (rothL deep dives) to Stage Two's s06, told here in two sentences only. Present the dispute over the Waterloo story by naming the conflict between this scene's deep dive (Drumont, an 'information advantage') and bc_s02 (Dairnvaell's 1846 pamphlet; the archive's 'just that: a legend'), and leave the full account to bc_s02. The 'Effects on Palestine/Region' and 'Machine Today' passages are interpretive readings: keep them only in a clearly labeled passage. Figures: power structure of the five houses; timeline of Mayer Amschel's life.

Palestine inside the Ottoman order, 1799–1840. Start from me_s01 and tk_s01 (one empire without internal borders, the millet system, the costs of non-Muslim status, Jerusalem district and parts of the Beirut and Damascus provinces, the 1831–40 Egyptian interlude), then the narrative: Napoleon at Acre in 1799 and the disputed 'proclamation to the Jews' (present the forgery case: Schwarzfuchs, Laurens, Schechter, Popkin, Akadem; and the other side: Gichon, Schur, the JVL's 'debated'); Ibrahim Pasha's conquest from 31 October 1831; the 1834 revolt with its dates and numbers (one in five conscripted, the Dung Gate entry of 19–20 May, 50/16/5 dead, Bayt Jala, Hebron with both casualty accounts, Qasim al-Ahmad's execution); the 1840 Convention of London, the bombardment of Acre on 3 November 1840 and Britain's stated interest. Give the Kimmerling–Migdal versus Morris dispute over the revolt and Palestinian identity in full, with Shamir and Manna. Mark Treaty of Lausanne (1923) as a later volume. Maps: turkey_arc and me_layers (Ottoman node only). Figure: timeline 1799–1840.

N M Rothschild & Sons as a creditor and contractor to the British state, in order: founded in London (1809 in this scene; 1811 in s01's rothL: give both and log the conflict), the £5 million Prussian loan of 1818 in sterling, the 1825 specie supply to the Bank of England, Lionel's seat in 1858 after the Jews Relief Act (elected since 1847), and the Suez purchase of November 1875 told from the research: 15 and 25 November dates, 44% of the shares, £4 million advanced while Parliament was not sitting, the 'technically unsecured' loan repaid within five months, Gladstone's objection, Disraeli's 'highway to our Indian Empire' and 'not a financial investment', and the disputed 15 per cent commission (both sides). Then the Waterloo legend: Dairnvaell's 1846 'Satan' pamphlet, Nathan's death in 1836, the archive's verdict and Ferguson's £7,000 ceiling; name it as antisemitic in origin. Note that the jwatte blog is the only citation for the archive's words and flag the claim as attributed. Link or_s01 (Stage Two) for the route to India. Figures: timeline 1809–1875; comparison of the legend and the record.

The Holy See as a borrower: Giovanni Torlonia as papal banker (ennobled 1794), the Torlonia–Orsini marriage of 1823, the 1831 arrangement with the Rothschilds, the 1832 loan of £400,000 to Gregory XVI, the Tosti affair of 1834, and the 1906 Jewish Encyclopedia phrase. From vat_s00d tell only what predates 1897: the Orsini and Colonna as Princes Assistant to the Papal Throne since 1735, the fall of the Papal States in 1870, and the Black Nobility's response; link forward for 1929. From bc_s08 give one sentence on the claimed chain to 2026 (Villa Torlonia, the 2026 IOR appointment) and link forward. oc_ch48 supplies a plain-language analogy (the 'singleton'); use its street version in one labeled passage, not the code. This scene contains internal conflicts the writer must present, not resolve: Tosti as embezzling treasurer vs. a cardinal's refinancing; Maria Luisa vs. Teresa Orsini; the London vs. Paris house as counterparty; Pauly's appointment on 25 March vs. 28 April 2026; Villa Torlonia from 1923 vs. 1925. Hold the discipline note at full strength: the Pauly link is institutional adjacency, not a family tie, and Catholic criticism that centred on the Rothschilds' Jewishness is named as antisemitism. Figure: timeline 1794–1870.

Protestant restorationism before Jewish political Zionism: Shaftesbury and Palmerston (1839–40; the instruction to the Constantinople embassy; the Jerusalem consulate with a brief to protect Jews), then the slogan's documented origin from sq_s05 (Alexander Keith, 1843; Shaftesbury, 1853; Zangwill's first Zionist use in 1901, linked forward) with the debate over whether it meant 'empty' or 'without a nation', then the Blackstone Memorial (March 1891; more than 400 signers including Rockefeller, Morgan and the Chief Justice). State plainly that most Jewish communal bodies of the period opposed or ignored restorationism, and that its motives were prophecy and empire. Tell sq_s05's other two claims (offers, 'religious war') only by a forward link. Link forward to Scofield (s05, Part One) and the christian_zionism map without embedding it. Figures: timeline 1839–1891; comparison of the British and American currents.

Reform from Istanbul and Palestinian society, 1839–1878: the Gülhane edict (3 November 1839) and its promises, the Reform Edict of 18 February 1856 and the Crimean War, the constitution of 23 December 1876 and the parliament of 19 March 1877, and Yusuf Diya al-Khalidi as Jerusalem's deputy and an opponent of Abdul Hamid II, exiled in 1878. This answers s01's claim that Palestinian delegates sat in the Ottoman parliament: say exactly what the record supports. Present both disputes (115 vs. 120 deputies; Khalidi's mayoralty dated 1865 or 1870). Article 62 of the Treaty of Berlin (1878) closes the section and points to rd0_limits. From dsp_s01 tell only the start of emigration to the Americas in the 1870s (Bethlehem, Beit Jala, Beit Sahour; Ottoman papers; 'Turcos'), linking forward for Chile, El Salvador and 1948. Link the Baseline's s00h for the Mutasarrifate of 1872 and the population of about 600,000 rather than retelling them. Mention the 1899 letter to Herzl only as a forward link. Figure: timeline 1839–1878. Told in full in another chapter of this library and only linked here: [scene:dsp_s01|...] (one or two sentences each, no retelling).

The 1858 Land Code as a legal mechanism: registration for revenue and conscription, cultivators who did not register, title in the names of village heads, urban notables and absentee families in Beirut and Damascus. Add the research: the 1858 Tabu law and the 1867 law on foreigners' property (Article II's equality clause, quoted from the 1898 US dispatch), Kark's 'urban effendis' and the 52 estate buildings that became cores of Jewish settlements and the 15 that became German Christian ones, Porath on appropriation by rich families, and Abufarha on why peasants avoided registration. Present the characterization dispute (a loophole exploited, per the Marmara thesis, vs. a wider privatization, per Kark). Tell the Sursock sales and the evictions only as the 1920s consequence, briefly, linking forward to Part One's s04j. Keep the scene's scope line: a legal form, not a cause. Figure: process flow from the 1858 law to a sellable deed (at most six steps).

The religious debate, presented and not decided: Jeremiah 29:7, the Three Oaths (Ketubot 110b–111a) and their three clauses, the reading that bars a state before the Messiah (Satmar's Vayoel Moshe, 1959; Neturei Karta; Agudat Israel, 1912, linked forward), and the opposite case (Nachmanides; Rav Abraham Isaac Kook; the arguments that the oaths lapsed or that Balfour and the League supplied the nations' consent). Add Reform's 1885 rejection and its later reversal, and close on where the debate stands today. Note for the audit: the citation w_kook points to a page on Hillel Kook, not Abraham Isaac Kook; do not rest any claim about Rav Kook on it alone. Figure: comparison of the two readings.

From prayer to program, 1840–1890: liturgical hope, then Alkalai after the 1840 Damascus affair, Kalischer (1862), Hess (1862) and Pinsker (1882) in one line each (s02 tells them in full), Hovevei Zion and the Kattowitz conference of 1884 under Pinsker, BILU's pioneers in 1882, and Birnbaum's coining of 'Zionism' in 1890. Name the recorded motives (persecution, the failure of emancipation, European nationalism, religious longing, and Christian restorationism from outside, linking bc_s05). Herzl came last: a movement already had groups before it had an organization. Note the irony the record shows: Pinsker, whose pamphlet did not insist on Palestine, chaired the Palestine-focused Kattowitz meeting. Figure: timeline 1840–1890.

The idea appears, 1862–1885: Hess and Rome and Jerusalem (1862) with its later rediscovery; the March 1881 assassination, the pogroms of 1881–84, the May Laws of 1882; Pinsker's Auto-Emancipation (1882) and its territorial agnosticism; the emigration of about two million, 90–95% to America and about 3% to Palestine (give the source and that these are estimates); Reform's Pittsburgh Platform of 1885 quoted from its text. Name the antisemitism plainly. The shemRoot and palSem entities: tell Schlözer's 1781 coinage and Marr's 1879 'antisemitism' in two sentences and link the Baseline's s00b and s00b0; state the genetics findings as the papers give them, and test palSem's claim that Arabs were 'named nowhere' in founding Zionist literature against palSem's own deep dive (Ahad Ha'am raised the concern in writing in 1891) and Herzl's 1895 diary (s03), so it is not overstated. Carry the Kishinev and 1917–21 figures only as forward context. Figure: key figures (two million, 90–95%, about 3%, 1882, 1885).

Who the Jews of Palestine were before Herzl. The Old Yishuv (about 24,000 in 1880, 13,900 of them in Jerusalem, per Barın; 23,000 per Elia) and its earlier growth; the 5 April 1870 firman for the Alliance Israélite Universelle's agricultural school at Jaffa (do not call it Mikveh Israel unless a source does); the First Aliyah from 1881–82 with each settlement's date (Petah Tikva 1878/1882 through Hadera 1891); the Yemenite arrivals of 1881–82 as the Jews of the Arab world entering this story; and Jewish opposition from inside (Jerusalem's Orthodox community reporting newcomers to the authorities; Jellinek's 'We are at home in Europe'). Present the dispute over numbers (20,000–30,000; 25,000; up to 60,000, with 50–70% leaving) and the end-of-period population (50,000, 55,000 or 80,000 by 1907). Figure: key figures; timeline of settlement founding.

The Ottoman state and the Arabs of Palestine respond, 1882–1896. Ottoman policy first, from the documents: the June and July 1882 decisions, the one-month and three-month pilgrim rules (Moore, 5 March 1887; Straus, 28 January and 19 May 1888, with the Grand Vizier's stated reasons and the US 'utterly repugnant' reply), the 14 June 1893 Foreign Office draft citing Article 62 of the Treaty of Berlin, the Grand Vizier's July 1893 assurance, and the 27 March 1894 note on 'the prevention of the permanent establishment in Palestine of Jewish immigrants'; then why the rules leaked (Capitulations, consular protection, Britain's 1847 declaration; more than 50,000 settled anyway). Present the dispute over when the land-sale ban began (1892, 1893/94 or March 1894). Then the Arab side as political agency: the peasants' first reactions, the 24 June 1891 petition (petition or telegram; Jerusalem alone or with Jaffa, both given), Muhammad Tahir al-Husayni and the 1893 Commission for Sale, Najib al-Hajj in 1895, and the 1897 freeze as a forward link; present the dispute over whether this opposition was political (Jewish Agency overview vs. Beška and Mandel). Do not conflate the 1834 mufti Tahir Afandi al-Husayni with Muhammad Tahir al-Husayni; the sources name them separately. From tk_s02 tell only the pre-1897 part (the restrictions; Herzl's pursuit of a charter from 1896) and link forward for the 1901 audience. Figures: timeline 1882–1896; comparison of what the Porte ordered and what happened.

Edmond de Rothschild's colonies and his refusal of Herzl. Use bc_s04 together with every Edmond deep-dive section in s01's rothP (James Mayer's Paris house; the 1882 Rishon LeZion appeal via Mohilever; the settlement table with dates and the naming of Zikhron Ya'akov and Mazkeret Batya; the administrators the colonists complained of; the JCA transfer; PICA from 1924 under his son James; Ramat HaNadiv; Ben-Gurion's 'builder of the Jewish Yishuv'). The July 1896 refusal comes from Herzl's diary (the 'rude telegram'; 'salvage everything'); s01's deep dive gives a different sequence (refused to receive him, then a meeting via an intermediary): present both. The figures in rothP ('$5–6 million', '~$200 million today', '~40% of early Yishuv capital', 'roughly 30 colonies') carry no citation: state that they are unsourced estimates or leave them out, and discuss money_1948:The Streams:0, whose first row records Edmond's colonies as 'Not totaled in the record'. Note the conflicting later dates (JCA transfer 1899 vs. PICA 1924; PICA's handover to the Jewish Agency in 1957 vs. Yad Hanadiv as successor). From pn_s01 use only the 'Rothschilds paid for it all' myth and the record that answers it, linking forward. Figures: comparison of the two Rothschilds (Walter and Edmond); embed money_1948:The Streams:0. Told in full in another chapter of this library and only linked here: [scene:pn_s01|...] (one or two sentences each, no retelling).

Baron Maurice de Hirsch and the Jewish Colonization Association: incorporation in London in September 1891, £2,000,000 authorized in £100 shares of which Hirsch took 19,993 of 20,000, the stated purpose quoted from the Jewish Encyclopedia, Moisés Ville (1889, Löwenthal) and the other colonies, about 6,757 colonists by 1896 and about 1,519,000 acres by 1939, 'productivization', and why Argentina was a refuge rather than a rival national project. Include the hardship record (typhus, food shortages, Sinay's book). The scene contradicts itself on Hirsch's death ('a year before Basel' vs. 'five years before'): Hirsch died in 1896 per the scene; Basel was 1897; present the date and drop the error. The further '£7,000,000' carries no separate citation: attribute or omit. Link forward to Edmond's 1899 transfer to the JCA (bc_s04). Figures: key figures; comparison of the JCA and political Zionism.

Dreyfus and Herzl, 1894–1896: the bordereau, Esterhazy, Devil's Island, Zola's 'J'accuse!' (January 1898) and rehabilitation in 1906 told briefly as consequence; Herzl's life to 1896 and the Dreyfus pivot as his diaries show it (years of development, the 1895 options); Der Judenstaat (February 1896) as the text says it, with gia_src_s01's quotation ('Shall we choose Palestine or Argentine? We shall take what is given us') and Avnery's reading. Check the scene's own errors before writing: the book entity says Der Judenstaat considered Uganda, but the Uganda offer came in 1903 (link forward to Part One's s04f); the date of the degradation ceremony and the crowd's words ('Death to the Jews' vs. 'À bas les Juifs') differ within the scene, so give both or the one a source fixes. Present the June 1895 diary passage on 'the penniless population' as the deep dive gives it, with Morris and Masalha on one side and the scholars who read it differently on the other; do not carry the deep dive's 'What is not disputed' sentence as settled. Give the four Jewish objections (Bund, Reform, Ahad Ha'am, Orthodox). The deep dive's 'Machine Today' and 'Effects' passages are interpretive readings and belong in a labeled passage or a forward link. Figures: timeline 1894–1896; comparison of what Der Judenstaat says and what is commonly claimed about it.

Closing synthesis: the board as it stood in 1896, piece by piece, as bc_s07 sets it (state, finance, church), adding the pieces the chapter has built: the Ottoman state that restricted Jewish entry and land purchase, Palestinian Arab society with its deputy, its notables and its 1891 petition, the Old Yishuv and the new colonies, and the Jewish movements and their Jewish critics. From vat_s01 give only the 1904 refusal and the 45 years of non-recognition as a forward link. Discuss year_ledger:Prelude:0 and the numbers in its rows (1881 pogroms; 1882 colonies; 1885 Pittsburgh), and point to the state_build map as where Part One begins. The synthesis figure is required: a power structure (at most four levels, eight boxes) of who could act on Palestine in 1896: the Porte, the European powers through the Capitulations, the Paris house, the JCA, the restorationist lobby, the Jerusalem notables. Figure: one synthesis power structure; embed year_ledger:Prelude:0.
